title: Cobalt Parcel peak capacity
brief: Cobalt Parcel's network planning lead, Rafael Ostrowski, needs a peak-season capacity summary for the operations directors, covering the peak window from 2026-11-23 to 2026-12-23. Five depots, with daily capacity and forecast peak daily volume in parcels, and utilization. Tulsa: 42000 capacity, 39600 forecast, 94.3 percent. Omaha: 36000, 28800, 80.0. Memphis: 55000, 57200, 104.0. Denver: 30000, 26100, 87.0. Boise: 18000, 14400, 80.0. Network total: 181000 capacity, 166100 forecast, 91.8 percent utilization, 14900 parcels of headroom. Memphis is the one depot over capacity, by 2200 parcels a day, and Tulsa has only 2400 of headroom, so the plan is to reroute 2200 Memphis parcels a day to Tulsa from 2026-11-23, which brings Memphis to exactly 100.0 percent and Tulsa to 99.5 percent, so both would be at their limit with no slack. Omaha could take up to 7200 more parcels a day but rerouting there adds a day of transit. Seasonal hiring is 640 people in total, 210 of them for Memphis. Sections: "Network at a glance", "Depot capacity", "Memphis and Tulsa plan" and "Risks". The risks to cover: any outage or weather delay at Memphis or Tulsa during the window has nowhere to go except Omaha, and the plan relies on all 640 seasonal workers starting by 2026-11-16.

edit.request: The Memphis forecast has been raised to 58000 parcels a day, which is 105.5 percent and 3000 over capacity, and the reroute to Tulsa becomes 2400 parcels a day.
